clue.text: Thanks to Shakespeare, a herald puts it on

parts.note: TA is informal British for thank you
Shakespeare is known as the Bard

explanation.surface: A herald dons something with Shakespeare's blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is the short emblazoned coat worn by a herald over armour or robes.

clue.text: South Indian visible in about a mile?

indicators.note: visible in says the letters can be seen inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man from southern India can be spotted about a mile off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are a people of south India and Sri Lanka, and the word also names their language.

clue.text: See 5
CC of the old order divides mythical bird and queen

indicators.note: divides says one piece splits the other apart by sitting inside it

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen
hest is an archaic word for a command, as in behest

explanation.surface: A cathedral city where an ancient decree comes between a fabulous bird and a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: CC throughout this puzzle means cathedral city; 'divides' signals the container. Hest is an archaic word solvers may not know, surviving in 'behest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester in Kent has one of England's oldest cathedrals, making it a cathedral city.

clue.text: Cockney openings may ginger things up

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker of London says the long A of the word openings like a long I

parts.note: openings are gaps or spaces

explanation.surface: Gaps in a London accent might liven things up.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney, the working-class London accent, 'spaces' comes out as 'spices'; 'Cockney' is the sound-alike signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spices are seasonings that add zest, which is what ginger does to food.

clue.text: Dear creature, awful bore, not even amounting to a CC

parts.note: a pet is a beloved animal

indicators.note: awful says the word bore is mangled into a new order

parts.note: something not even is uneven, or rough

explanation.surface: A beloved animal, a dreadful bore, and uneven too, adds up to a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' turns BORE into ERBO; 'amounting to' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Peterborough in Cambridgeshire has a great Norman cathedral, so it ranks as a cathedral city.

clue.text: CC concluding others

explanation.surface: A cathedral city that brings others to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition: this city's name forms the ending of other place names such as Manchester, Winchester and Rochester.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester in Cheshire is a cathedral city, and its name is the closing part of several other city names in this grid.

clue.text: CC for skipper grasping a lot of Portuguese capital

indicators.note: grasping says the fish holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: the saury is a long-beaked fish also called the skipper

indicators.note: a lot of says most of the city name is used, its end dropped

parts.note: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal

explanation.surface: A ship's captain clutching much of Lisbon's wealth stands for a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipper' suggests a ship's captain but is the fish, otherwise called a saury. 'a lot of' cuts the last two letters from the capital, and 'grasping' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Salisbury in Wiltshire has a famous cathedral with England's tallest spire.

clue.text: Holding movement sets me back a couple

indicators.note: back says the word me is read from right to left

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds

explanation.surface: A move to grip someone costs me a pair of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets me back' reads like a cost, but only 'back' signals the reversal of 'me'; 'sets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrace is a hug, a movement of the arms that holds someone close.

clue.text: Church's part to soak the French?

parts.note: to steep is to soak in liquid
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Is soaking the French part of church business?
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tower and spire of a church building.

clue.text: Grotesque monster keeps company — warning of gales ahead

indicators.note: keeps says the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside
grotesque says the word monster is distorted into a new shape

explanation.surface: A hideous beast holds onto a firm, a sign of stormy weather on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grotesque' makes STORMNE from MONSTER, and 'keeps' puts CO in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm cone is a canvas cone hoisted at coastguard stations as a signal that a gale is expected.

clue.text: CC provides a variety of lectures: go!

indicators.note: a variety of says the letters that follow are mixed into another order

explanation.surface: A city offers a range of talks, so off you go!
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of' rearranges LECTURES plus GO; 'provides' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloucester has a great medieval cathedral, making it a cathedral city.

clue.text: International trial

explanation.surface: An experiment carried out across nations.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test is an international cricket or rugby match, and a test is also any trial or examination.

clue.text: Something higher than I could be a myth

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the following words might form something else

explanation.surface: Anything loftier than me is probably made up.
explanation.walkthrough: MY HAT is an exclamation of surprise, but the definition reads it literally: a hat sits above the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat worn on the head is the part of a person above them, so it is higher than the wearer.

clue.text: Becoming less recalcitrant at length during grass work

indicators.note: during says one piece goes in the middle of the other

parts.note: mowing is the work of cutting grass
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Someone grows more agreeable over time while cutting the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at length' looks like 'eventually', but 'length' is the old cloth measure and 'during' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Mellowing means growing softer and more relaxed in temperament, less stubborn.

clue.text: It's odd about love — a dress takes the place of flowers

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other pieces

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar
O is love, a zero score in tennis
a sari is a draped Indian dress

explanation.surface: Something strange is going on: a dress replaces flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the place of' looks like a substitution instruction, but 'place of flowers' is the definition and 'takes' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosarium is a rose garden, a garden where flowers are grown.

clue.text: Tell us who will make a CC

indicators.note: will make says the letters of the words before are formed into something new

explanation.surface: Tell us who is going to create a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Southwell in Nottinghamshire is a small town with a minster that is the cathedral of its diocese.

clue.text: Choose to have a lot of money and power?

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote

indicators.note: a lot of says only a portion of the word is kept, its end dropped

parts.note: riches are money and wealth

explanation.surface: Opting for great wealth and influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' keeps the first three letters of the wealth word; 'to have' links. The definition is the noun sense, as in 'the electric is off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric is used as a noun for electricity, the domestic power supply.

clue.text: Fuel has power to contain drink

parts.note: coke is a solid fuel made from coal
can means is able, has the power

explanation.surface: A fuel is able to hold a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Coke can is the metal container a cola drink comes in.

clue.text: One with which imp goes scot-free?

explanation.surface: Something a little devil carries with it when getting away unpunished.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition: IMP placed before this word gives IMPUNITY, freedom from punishment, so it is what an imp has when going scot-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity is oneness, the state of being one; impunity means escaping without penalty.

clue.text: Lift up hearts in part of church?

parts.note: a spire is the pointed top of a church tower

explanation.surface: Raising spirits while up in a church tower.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is to uplift and encourage people's spirits.

clue.text: CC with a golden sovereign: on your head be it!

parts.note: C with a bar over it is the shorthand for the Latin cum, with, used in prescriptions
or is the heraldic name for gold
K is short for king, a sovereign

explanation.surface: A city with a gold coin, whose fate rests on your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on your head be it!' adds a second hint: cork is worn on the head, as in cork-lined sun helmets. Cork in Ireland is a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cork, in southern Ireland, has St Fin Barre's Cathedral, making it a cathedral city.

clue.text: "The Gun and Bottle", once a capital CC

explanation.surface: An old pub sign names a former seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the Winchester rifle, the large Winchester bottle used for chemicals, and the city that was capital of Wessex and of early England.
explanation.definitionFit: The rifle and the bottle both carry this name, and the Hampshire cathedral city was once England's capital.

clue.text: CC of Sci-fi

explanation.surface: A city known for science fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: H. G. Wells wrote The Time Machine and The War of the Worlds; the city of Wells in Somerset has a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells in Somerset is England's smallest cathedral city, and H. G. Wells was a pioneer of science fiction.

clue.text: Poem, for example, in a CC

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation goes inside the city name

parts.note: Ely in Cambridgeshire is a cathedral city
EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A poem, for instance, set in a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, typically a lament for the dead.

clue.text: CC finished in the theatre

explanation.surface: A city that came to an end at a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: President Abraham Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre in 1865.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln has a great cathedral, and the president of that name was assassinated at a theatre.

clue.text: Make a bit of noise-in a month I'm going to be fifty

parts.note: DEC abbreviates December
the speaker gives I
taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone about to turn fifty next month making some noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' only links I and BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decibel is a unit of loudness, so one is a small measure of noise.

clue.text: God needs you to write even letters from Agra in Persian

indicators.note: even letters from says to take the second, fourth and so on of the words after

explanation.surface: A deity requires you to write certain characters from an Indian city in Persian.
explanation.walkthrough: From AGRA take G, A; from IN PERSIAN take N, E, S, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganesa, the elephant-headed Hindu deity of wisdom and new beginnings.

clue.text: Nodding to agent general inside

indicators.note: inside says the general goes within the agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: Nodding to a spy with a general within.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nodding is dozing off, drowsy and half asleep.
